tools.name: memory_status
tools.description: Check what this session is bound to: store, tenant, principal, project and the current history id. Call it first in a session, or when a call fails with history_changed, before retrying anything. Read-only; it never authorizes a model request.

tools.name: memory_capture
tools.description: Remember something you observed: an error, a test result, a decision, a fact with its source. Give a stable `key` and `request.source_event` for the same event so a retry replays instead of duplicating; the same key with different text is a conflict. Text is stored as untrusted evidence, not as an instruction.

tools.name: memory_handoff
tools.description: Pass a task to another principal with their current permissions: `prepare` a handoff from a checkpoint, `preview` what the recipient would receive, `materialize` it as the recipient, `ack` or `cancel`. A handoff never widens access; what the recipient cannot see is left out and reported.

tools.name: memory_brief
tools.description: Ask for a briefing before starting work: `brief` with a short query returns mandatory constraints, ranked guidance with sources and a receipt. Read `status` and `reason` first: `blocked` or `budget_insufficient` means decide, not truncate. `rerun` repeats an earlier receipt with a new query. Project, bindings, budget and tokenizer default to the session's.

format.description: json (default) returns the structured packet; text returns a cited Markdown rendering in a compact envelope with the same receipt.

tools.name: memory_fetch
tools.description: Follow up on a briefing you already have: `fetch` more of a source, `receipt` the diagnostics behind a receipt, `replay` the exact bytes that were delivered, `receipts` to list recent ones. Replays can report expired or purged; that is an answer, not an error to retry.

format.description: json (default) returns the structured packet; text returns a cited Markdown rendering in a compact envelope with the same receipt.

tools.name: memory_checkpoint
tools.description: Save progress before you stop or hand over: objective, current state, next actions, failed attempts, blockers and verification gaps, under a project, task and expected revision. Use the exact revision you last saw; a conflict means someone else saved first, so resume and merge rather than overwrite.

weight.description: Declared relative criterion weight; absent means 1. Weight changes alter the scope denominator, not evidence validity.

expected_revision.description: The revision last seen; null accepts the current revision without a compare-and-set check.

readers.description: Who may read the checkpoint; null keeps the stream's current readers (the writer alone on a first save).

format.description: json (default) returns the structured packet; text returns a cited Markdown rendering in a compact envelope with the same receipt.

tools.name: memory_resume
tools.description: Pick up a saved task: returns the checkpoint, open operations and the context you are still authorized to see, within a token budget. Read `status`; a `blocked` or `partial` packet lists what is missing. Budget and tokenizer default to the session's.

weight.description: Declared relative criterion weight; absent means 1. Weight changes alter the scope denominator, not evidence validity.

expected_revision.description: The revision last seen; null accepts the current revision without a compare-and-set check.

readers.description: Who may read the checkpoint; null keeps the stream's current readers (the writer alone on a first save).

format.description: json (default) returns the structured packet; text returns a cited Markdown rendering in a compact envelope with the same receipt.

tools.name: memory_plan
tools.description: Track a multi-step plan on a task: `plan_save` creates or revises the whole plan (phases, steps with stable ids, prerequisites), `plan_step` updates one step's status, notes and evidence, `plan_get` reads the current or an earlier revision with computed progress, `plan_list` pages the project's plans. A step counts as done only with evidence; a changed definition needs fresh evidence. Progress is recorded work, not independent certification.

weight.description: Declared relative criterion weight; absent means 1. Weight changes alter the scope denominator, not evidence validity.

expected_revision.description: The revision last seen; null accepts the current revision without a compare-and-set check.

readers.description: Who may read the checkpoint; null keeps the stream's current readers (the writer alone on a first save).

format.description: json (default) returns the structured packet; text returns a cited Markdown rendering in a compact envelope with the same receipt.

tools.name: memory_feedback
tools.description: Report what happened after using memory: `outcome` records the result of a run with its evidence, `feedback` rates whether a specific memory helped. This informs ranking; it cannot activate a procedure or change policy.
